chunks: 1017 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed Ẓuhr as five rakʿahs. He said: “If he does not know whether he sat in the fourth or did not sit, then let him count four rakʿahs of it as the Ẓuhr prayer, and let him sit and recite the tashahhud. Then he should pray, while sitting, two rakʿahs and four sajdahs, and add them to the fifth, so that it becomes a nafilah prayer.”

key_terms.الرَّابِعَةِ: the fourth rakʿah, whose sitting is in question
key_terms.رَكَعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs to be prayed while sitting
key_terms.سَجَدَاتٍ: prostrations performed as part of the corrective action

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he prays five rakʿahs for Ẓuhr by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who accidentally performs five rakʿahs in Ẓuhr prayer and is uncertain whether he sat in the fourth rakʿah. The Imam عليه السلام instructs how to preserve the obligation as four rakʿahs and transform the extra rakʿah into a nafilah through seated prayer and sajdahs, showing the detailed fiqh of sahw in salat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1017 - Al-Ala reported from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"I asked him about a man who prayed Dhuhr five rak'ahs. He said: 'If he does not know whether he sat in the fourth rak'ah or not, let him treat it as four rak'ahs for the Dhuhr prayer, then he should sit, perform the tashahhud, and then pray two rak'ahs while sitting and perform four sajdahs. He should then add these to the fifth rak'ah, and it will be considered a nafl (voluntary) prayer.'"
